newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico establishes Ciudad Juarez natgas region.
newsitem.headline: Mexico establishes Ciudad Juarez natgas region.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE) said on Monday it set up the area surrounding Ciudad Juarez, Chihuahua state as a region to be auctioned for private natural gas distribution.

The announcement, published in the government's Official Gazette, is part of Mexico's privatization of natural gas distribution. Transport of the fuel was formerly dominated by state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex), which will retain control of production.

The CRE did not say when it will open the region's bidding or when bids are due. It generally chooses the winner on the basis of the lowest client distribution price offered and the most residential clients committed to serve within five years.
Ciudad Juarez had a population of more than 789,000 people in 1990, and is expected to grow to 1.61 million by the year 2010, according to census counts.
The region is a key maquiladora (in-bond) site, representing 2.14 percent of the national maquiladora output. It has 14 industrial parks and several other industrial corridors.
Average natural gas consumption in the region is 4.312 billion kilocalories or 18 million cubic feet per day (cfd), according to Pemex. The CRE said 64,600 industrial clients use natural gas.
Fuel oil consumption is about 5,003 million kilocalories or 20.88 million cfd. "Natural gas can be used easily as a substitute for the fuel," the CRE said.
CRE President Hector Olea has said U.S. distributors could provide natural gas to the region through private pipelines.
